_comment: Where the sky is dark enough to sleep under. Drawn as an overlay on the map.
EMPTY ON PURPOSE. The stop list sat here as a placeholder for twenty sessions
and got treated as real; this one ships empty instead, and the Sky button does
not appear on the map until there are zones in it. No data is better than data
nobody approved.
SCHEMA
zones: [ {
bortle: 1..4     Bortle class. Only 1-4 are worth drawing — 5 and up is
suburban sky and you will not see the Milky Way.
1  no light pollution at all, zodiacal light visible
2  truly dark, Milky Way highly structured
3  rural, some glow on the horizon
4  rural/suburban transition, Milky Way visible but washed
name:   string   what the place is called, for the map label and the sheet
ring:   [[lat, lon], ...]   one closed-ish outer ring, same [lat, lon] order
as usa.json outline. Do not repeat the first point at the
end; the renderer closes it.
Optional per zone:
sqm:    number   sky brightness in mag/arcsec^2, if you have the real figure
note:   string   anything about access, e.g. whether you can legally park
RULES THAT WILL BITE
1. Keep rings SIMPLIFIED. This ships in the app and is drawn on every map
repaint. Budget roughly 40 points per zone and no more than ~60 zones;
past that the repaint after a pinch starts to show.
2. Coordinates are [lat, lon], NOT GeoJSON's [lon, lat]. Every published
light-pollution dataset you will convert from is GeoJSON, so this is the
mistake to expect — a swapped pair puts the Mojave in the Indian Ocean.
3. Rings must not self-intersect. The renderer fills with nonzero winding and
a bow-tie will fill the wrong half.
4. Cover the ROUTE CORRIDOR, not the country. Zones more than a couple of
hours off the road are weight in the app for no benefit.
WHERE THE DATA COMES FROM — unresolved, and it is the research job
The standard source is the World Atlas of Artificial Night Sky Brightness
(Falchi et al. 2016), derived from VIIRS. It is a raster, so turning it into
these rings means contouring it. IMPORTANT: it is licensed CC BY-NC — fine
for a personal trip, but it must be attributed, and that rules out anything
commercial. Named IDA International Dark Sky Places are a separate, much
smaller source and are points rather than areas.
Whatever is used, record it in `source` below so the next person can check it.
